ac.title: Armor Class (AC)
ac.text: How hard something is to hit. Lower is better: AC 10 is unarmored, AC 0 is nearly untouchable. This is the old tabletop convention.

hd.title: Hit Dice (HD)
hd.text: A rough measure of toughness. Each hit die adds about 4-5 hit points, and tougher monsters are worth more experience.

xp.title: Experience (XP)
xp.text: Points earned by defeating monsters. Enough XP raises your level.

morale.title: Morale
morale.text: How willing a monster is to keep fighting. Low-morale creatures flee when hurt; undead never do.

undead.title: Undead
undead.text: Creatures animated after death. They don't flee, don't sleep, and are often vulnerable to holy magic.

shout.title: Shout
shout.text: Heard by everyone in the same area, like a village bell. Use 'gossip' to reach every area.

gossip.title: Gossip
gossip.text: A global chat channel that reaches every player in every area.

mode.title: Modes
mode.text: 'mode commodore' gives the bare 40-column experience with no hints. 'mode modern' turns tips and stats back on.

mana.title: Mana (MP)
mana.text: The energy spells cost. It grows with your level and recovers slowly while you rest.

spell.title: Spells
spell.text: Learn them from trainers ('learn') or by reading scrolls ('learn <scroll>'), then 'cast <spell> [target]'. Higher-level spells need a higher level to learn.

class.title: Class
class.text: Your calling decides your HP and mana growth, how fast you improve at hitting, and which spells you can learn. Warriors hit best, mages cast most, clerics sit in between.

gold.title: Gold (gp)
gold.text: Money. Monsters and quests pay it; shops sell gear for it and buy your loot at half price.

food.title: Food and hunger
food.text: Your food meter drains over time (dwarves faster, elves slower). Hungry slows healing; Starving stops it; Famished hurts you. 'eat' bread, sausage, cheese or ale from the tavern.

race.title: Race
race.text: Your race adjusts HP, mana, hunger and how fast you learn. Dwarves are tough but hungry; elves are magical and frugal; humans learn faster.

corpse.title: Death and corpses
corpse.text: When you die you wake in the Hall of Second Chances. Everything you carried (except soulbound items) and your gold stay in a corpse where you fell. Only you can loot it for an hour; then it rots into a pile anyone can take. Type 'corpse' to see where yours is.

loot.title: Loot
loot.text: Monsters drop items on the floor, reserved for whoever fought them for 30 seconds. Use 'loot' or 'get all'. Uncollected drops crumble after 5 minutes. Weight limits what you can carry.

weight.title: Weight
weight.text: Everything weighs something. Your capacity is 30 + 5 per level, plus or minus your race (dwarves carry more). 'i' shows your load.

deathsdoor.title: Death's Door
deathsdoor.text: The first blow that would kill you in a fight leaves you at 1 HP instead. You then have one chance to 'flee' (90% to escape) or heal. A second lethal blow kills you: you wake in the Hall of Second Chances, and your belongings stay with your corpse.

wimpy.title: Wimpy
wimpy.text: 'wimpy 30' makes you flee automatically when your HP falls to 30% or less. Fleeing can fail, so don't lean on it.

talk.title: Talking
talk.text: 'talk <name>' starts a conversation with someone in the room. Pick numbered replies; 'leave' ends it. Some conversations pay out once, like a free ale for good manners.
